steps.text: Heat cream in a small saucepan until small bubbles appear around the edges. Remove from the heat and stir in sugar until it dissolves. Transfer mixture to a medium bowl and allow to cool, about 10 minutes.
Blend avocado and cream cheese in a food processor until smooth. Add lime juice and process until smooth.
Whisk blended avocado mixture into cooled cream mixture, then pour into an ice cream maker. Freeze according to the manufacturer's instructions, about 20 minutes.

Spoon avocado mixture into the prepared pie crust; smooth the surface with a spatula. Freeze until solid, at least 2 hours. Let cheesecake sit at room temperature until slightly softened yet firm enough to slice before serving, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Avocado Lime Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: This Mexican-inspired avocado and lime cheesecake recipe is easy to make with a ready-made graham cracker crust and homemade frozen avocado-lime custard.

review.reviewBody: Turned out great, I skipped the ice cream making part because I don't have one . I just poured it in the shell and froze. it went quick at the party though it tasted more like key lime pie, you couldn't really taste the avocados

I made this, slightly tweaked! I took 2 avocados, 1 small tub of light cool whip, juice from 2 limes, 1 can evaporated milk, just under 2/3 cup sugar and mixed it really well in our vitamix (I'm sure any blender would work great) to smooth it out and poured it into a ready made graham cracker crust and froze it. It turned out wonderful and was super easy!! :)

Cinco de Mayo in SC. I used 1/2 cup buttermilk (instead of cream cheese) and used a little less sugar (used ~2/3 cup). Turned out great and was lighter in calories.. I also did not heat the cream first, just blended all ingredients prior to adding them to the ice cream maker.
Loved it! Did not use ice cream maker. I just put it in the freezer for a few hrs. Everyone loved it, no one believed it had avocado in it. I cut the sugar in half (personal choice)

Very good pie. As others have stated, it's more like a key lime pie verses a cheesecake. I used 3 packages of cream cheese and 2 full avocados. These changes thickened the mix and yielded 2 pies. I also froze the pies in the freezer, as I do not own an ice cream maker.

Excellent dessert for taco night!! Super fresh and light! I didn't have an ice cream maker so just played it by ear. Didn't use a crust either (no graham crackers in Australia!!) so instead, after prepping the cream and processing the avos/cheese/lime, I whisked the two together and poured them into little ramekins and froze them - 6 hours later they were rock solid (possibly sooner didn't check). Moved them into the fridge and 1 hour later they were perfect. Garnished with thin candied lime and chopped pistachios (you eat with your eyes too!) Only negative is that you can barely taste the avocados. I used just over half of the lime juice needed, so if you want to taste the avos maybe use even less. Still it is amazing!

I have made this recipe and it is amazing. However, I made some adjustments and substitutions. I used 2 avocados, 2/3 cup of key lime juice, I substituted 14 oz. of fat free sweetened condensed milk for the cream, I added a tsp. of grated lime zest to amp up the lime flavor and divided the mixture among 12 individual graham cracker crusts and popped them in the freezer for two hours. Serve with some cool whip and a sprinkle of finely chopped pistachios! Yum!!My husband hates avocado, but he gobbled up two of these delicious tarts and had no idea!

Thank you for a delicious recipe! I was skeptical, but this is amazing! I'm not a fan of key lime pie because it is typically too tart, but this was just right!! I got tired of squeezing limes and getting hardly any juice, so I used about 1/4 cup of fresh lime juice and subbed in the stuff from the plastic lime for the other 1/4 cup. Still amazing!! I also made my own graham cracker crust. I did not use an ice cream maker. I processed everything in the food processor until smooth and then poured it into the pie crust and froze overnight.

I made this for a dinner party. The guests loved it! I didn't put the full amount of lime juice, but it still tasted great. Also, I didn't have an ice cream maker. Instead I used my emulsifier and froze in the freezer. It worked well.

Fabulous! I made per recipe originally, with an ice cream maker, then made two more pies for Bunco night...adding 2 tsp lime zest to bump up the lime flavor. I did make the cream/sugar mix the night before and chilled, and used chilled ripe avocados to help it freeze up faster, and it worked well. This is a keeper and so creamy...
This is so amazing! Everyone loves it. After the cream and sugar cool I toss everything into the blender then into the pie shell. EASY impressive dessert.
It was amazing... We used key lime juice...

I made this to take to an Easter gathering. This was a great HIT. everyone raved about it. I will be making it again in a couple weeks for a birthday party. As far as the recipe, I did make 2 changes. I never use sugar, so I substituted 1/2 cup Truvia sugar instead of the 3/4 cup regular sugar. Also, I bought 4 limes and this was not nearly enough to make 1/2 cup juice, so I used lime juice from concentrate that I had on hand.
This was delicious and you would never know it was made with avocado. Tasted just like a keylime pie
Best dessert ever to follow up a Mexican meal! The flavor is so bright and cool and refreshing.
So yum and refreshing. I would make the filling again just as Ice cream. I just froze it then blended and refroze. No one knew it was avocados. I personally love avocados, but the others don’t.
Used 1/3 fat cream cheese and it still tasted great!
I don't have an ice cream maker either so I just froze it in the pie shell. It was delicious. I also had a little extra so I put froze it and made a couple popsicles which were also good.
This cheese cake was delicious. I highly recommend it.

This is fabulous... Tart but not to tart and super refreshing in the hot weather. I will make this again and again. Made it exactly as the recipe said and I wouldn't change a thing. I did use fresh limes and I know it had to be better than just using lime juice. Kids weren't to sure about it. Liked the initial taste but said it had an odd after taste. I didn't get that at all. Of course husband had told them it was made with avocados so they were expecting it to be different. I loved it and so did the husband.
